decision_reason: Iteration 1 (only iter1_q1 was executed out of 4 planned queries) successfully identified the primary CDC FluView Week 40 report and a Mississippi state-level PDF — both directly covering the task window (Sept 29 – Oct 5, 2024). However, three planned queries (iter1_q2, iter1_q3, iter1_q4) were never executed. Key gaps remain: (1) no WHO/PAHO international corroboration, (2) no news-source evidence quotes, (3) no additional state-level subnational data beyond Mississippi, (4) no pediatric mortality or hospitalization rate data confirmed from a second source, and (5) the H5N1 California cases mentioned in the Week 40 snippet warrant a targeted follow-up. One more iteration with up to 4 queries will close these gaps and satisfy the stop condition (primary CDC source confirmed + at least one corroborating international or news source).

Three of four planned iteration-1 queries were not executed.

Results are dominated by cdc.gov (6/8 results), with one state health department (Mississippi) and one outdated local health district PDF (Washoe County 2023-24 season — wrong year). No international organization sources, no news sources, and no additional state health departments for the 2024-25 Week 40 window have been found yet.
trustworthiness_assessment: High for the two on-target results: CDC FluView Week 40 (cdc.gov, official U.S. surveillance) and Mississippi MSDH Week 40 PDF (msdh.ms.gov, official state health department). The Washoe County result (nnph.org) is from the 2023-24 season and is out of scope. The other CDC results (weeks 38, 51, and 2025 weeks) are off-target temporally and should not be used as evidence for the task window.
disease_location_time_fit_assessment: The top two results are an excellent fit: CDC FluView Week 40 ending October 5, 2024 (exact task window, national U.S.) and Mississippi MSDH Week 40 Sept 29–Oct 5, 2024 (exact task window, subnational). The remaining 6 results are either wrong season (2023-24), wrong week (38, 51), or future dates (2025) and do not fit the task window.
corroboration_potential_assessment: Moderate-to-high. WHO/PAHO weekly influenza updates for the Americas routinely include U.S. data and would corroborate CDC figures. News articles from early October 2024 citing CDC Week 40 data would provide evidence quotes. Additional state health department Week 40 reports (e.g., California given the H5N1 mention, or large states like Texas, New York, Florida) would expand subnational coverage. These are all achievable with targeted queries.

coverage_assessment: Core coverage is strong. The CDC FluView Week 40 report (week ending October 5, 2024) is confirmed as a candidate source and directly covers the task window at the national level with virus subtype data, positivity rates, and H5N1 case notes. The Mississippi state PDF explicitly covers Sept. 29–Oct. 5, 2024 with ILI rate data (2.8% state ILI rate, up from 2.3% prior week). PAHO results appeared (paho.org, iris.paho.org) for international corroboration, though the specific PAHO snippet retrieved is from December 2025 and is out of scope — the PAHO domain presence suggests a Week 40 2024 PAHO update may exist but was not surfaced in snippet form. State-level domains (health.ny.gov, dshs.texas.gov) appeared as candidates for subnational data. CIDRAP provides a credible secondary analytical source. The primary gap is that no Week 40 2024-specific PAHO or news snippet was confirmed in the metadata — however, the CDC FluView Week 40 source alone is sufficient as the gold-standard primary source for the task, and the Mississippi PDF provides confirmed subnational evidence. The max iteration bound prevents further refinement.
source_diversity_assessment: Moderate-to-good diversity across source types: official federal (CDC FluView), official state (Mississippi MSDH, New York DOH, Texas DSHS), international organization (PAHO — though specific Week 40 2024 snippet not confirmed), academic/news (CIDRAP). The two highest-value confirmed candidates are: (1) cdc.gov/fluview/surveillance/2024-week-40.html — official CDC FluView weekly report, gold-standard U.S. influenza surveillance, directly titled and dated for the task window; (2) msdh.ms.gov PDF — official Mississippi State Department of Health influenza surveillance report, explicitly dated "Sept. 29 – Oct. 5, 2024."
